title: SITF technique coverage reconciliation
claim_boundary: This repository profile records direct or partial reference-control coverage against a pinned threat taxonomy. It is not a compliance claim, organization adoption result, or proof that an attack technique is completely mitigated.

endpoint.limitation: Repository fixtures do not prove live endpoint fleet enrollment, telemetry health, phishing resistance, network enforcement, or incident recovery.

vcs.limitation: Repository fixtures do not prove live source-provider policy, read-event completeness, service patching, backups, or organization-wide enforcement.

cicd.limitation: Repository fixtures do not prove hosted-provider isolation, live credential policy, service availability, cache integrity, or fleet-wide workflow adoption.

registry.limitation: Consumer-side verification does not prevent all malicious publication, prove live registry patching, or establish backup and disaster-recovery readiness.

production.limitation: Local policies and fixtures do not prove live cloud authorization, production inventory completeness, data-plane DLP, sensor health, or disaster recovery.

techniques.rationale: Application approval, endpoint detection, and default-deny dependency script execution directly reduce unreviewed code execution on a developer endpoint.

techniques.remaining_work: Verify mail and browser phishing controls, endpoint-originated token binding, alert delivery, and incident response with live evidence.
techniques.rationale: EDR and phishing-resistant source authentication are supporting layers, but the repository does not directly verify endpoint phishing prevention and detection.
Secret-free workspaces and approved protected credential stores directly constrain local credential harvesting.

techniques.remaining_work: Add endpoint data classification, bulk-access detection, destination-aware DLP, and tested containment for local source and customer data.
techniques.rationale: Read-only shared workspaces and sensitive-file detection reduce exposure but do not prevent an already-compromised endpoint from harvesting local data.

techniques.remaining_work: Verify endpoint CPU, GPU, process, and energy anomaly detection plus automated containment without relying only on generic EDR enrollment.
techniques.rationale: EDR enrollment is relevant but no exact cryptomining detection or endpoint resource-abuse assertion exists.

techniques.remaining_work: Deny and detect runner registration from developer endpoints and correlate registration authority to an approved ephemeral runner inventory.
techniques.rationale: Socket exposure and runner registration authority are bounded separately, but no check proves that a workstation cannot be enrolled as a runner.
Resource-restricted, short-lived, phishing-resistant, and revocable source credentials directly constrain abuse of endpoint-held VCS access.

techniques.remaining_work: Inventory and govern developer-held CI/CD sessions and API credentials, including phishing resistance, scope, lifetime, revocation, and endpoint binding.
techniques.rationale: Privileged control-plane actor and session checks cover reviewed changes, not all local CI/CD credentials available after endpoint compromise.
Credential isolation, default-deny networking, exact extension identity, and bounded tool effects directly constrain abuse of local AI development tools.

techniques.remaining_work: Add immutable endpoint configuration backups, destructive-action detection, rebuild objectives, and tested fleet recovery evidence.
techniques.rationale: Encrypted backups are supporting evidence, but their recoverability and resistance to attacker-triggered endpoint destruction are not verified.
The Python source verifier directly rejects directional and invisible formatting controls plus non-ASCII and normalization-unstable identifiers, while malformed or incomplete analysis fails closed.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect local proxy listeners, tunneled egress, destination changes, and long-lived relay traffic, then verify containment and evidence retention.
techniques.rationale: Endpoint allowlisting and EDR are supporting controls but do not provide an exact SOCKS proxy detection assertion.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect hidden desktop services, injected UI processes, unauthorized screen capture, and remote-control channels with tested response.
techniques.rationale: Disabled debug services and EDR reduce exposure but do not specifically verify HVNC prevention or detection.

techniques.remaining_work: Classify and detect unauthorized WebRTC signaling, STUN/TURN access, and peer channels while preserving approved collaboration traffic.
techniques.rationale: Approved destinations and EDR provide partial support but no WebRTC C2-specific evidence.

techniques.remaining_work: Pin IDE and browser extension update identities, verify publisher signatures and update provenance, and revoke compromised versions fleet-wide.
techniques.rationale: Approved applications and immutable AI extensions are relevant, but the general extension auto-update channel is not verified.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect unauthorized blockchain clients, RPC endpoints, domain resolution, and embedded payload retrieval used as a control channel.
techniques.rationale: Allowlisted egress and EDR are supporting layers without blockchain-based C2-specific assertions.

techniques.remaining_work: Add identity- and process-aware egress policy plus behavioral detection for approved SaaS services used by unauthorized binaries as C2.
techniques.rationale: A destination allowlist alone cannot distinguish legitimate use from C2 over an approved service.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect DHT protocol use, unexpected UDP peer traffic, and embedded command retrieval while accounting for sanctioned peer-to-peer tools.
techniques.rationale: Generic egress and EDR coverage does not directly verify BitTorrent DHT C2 detection.

techniques.remaining_work: Inventory OAuth grants, constrain tenant and organization audience, detect cross-organization token use, and automate grant revocation.
techniques.rationale: Approved OAuth and credential ownership are covered for GitHub MCP, but cross-organizational OAuth abuse is not generally enforced.
Resource-restricted tokens, phishing-resistant login, hardware-protected SSH keys, and automated revocation directly constrain credential abuse for VCS access.
Enforced signed commits and repository-owned Git configuration directly make unsigned or wrongly attributed imposter commits rejectable.

techniques.remaining_work: Verify repository read authorization, bulk-clone and archive-download detection, egress controls, and attributable response for sensitive repositories.
techniques.rationale: Domain-anchored public exposure monitoring and scoped credentials reduce some stored-secret exposure, but an authorized read session can still exfiltrate non-public repository content.

techniques.remaining_work: Define ownership and monitoring for work-related personal repositories, forks, archives, and tokens without assuming enterprise controls cover personal accounts.
techniques.rationale: Owned-domain API and browser searches can surface some public personal repositories and forks, but personal repository read and export activity remains outside the current evidence boundary.

techniques.remaining_work: Verify VCS server and client version inventory, vulnerability intelligence, patch deadlines, compensating isolation, and patch-failure evidence.
techniques.rationale: The scanner interface is integrity verified, but no control applies it to VCS platform vulnerability management.

techniques.remaining_work: Enforce repository visibility changes through independent approval and provider audit alerts, then correlate newly public repositories with exposure monitoring.
techniques.rationale: Privileged-change evidence can bind reviewed configuration changes and public monitoring can detect some domain-anchored content after exposure, but neither currently proves provider-side prevention or alerting for every visibility change.

techniques.remaining_work: Add complete repository read audit, archive and clone volume thresholds, network context, alert delivery, and response for sensitive repositories.
techniques.rationale: Credential scope and lifecycle audit reduce access, but they do not detect use of valid read authority to clone sensitive repositories.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect compromised organization accounts creating or repurposing repositories for payload hosting, including releases, Pages, and workflow artifacts.
techniques.rationale: Public API and browser exposure review covers domain-anchored content but does not directly identify malicious repository hosting after account compromise or comprehensively inspect Releases and Pages.

GitHub deletion and critical-ref restrictions, GitHub-admin-independent retained backups, and real isolated restore drills directly reduce repository mass-deletion impact; audit containment and live organization adoption remain external integration requirements.
Untrusted changes remain unprivileged and protected source changes bind an exact target and before-after state to independent approval.
Protected reference changes are bound to reviewed control-plane evidence and release consumers reject silent trust-signal downgrades.
Exact pull-request revision binding, blocked cross-run elevation, separate trusted execution, and complete fork-network evidence directly address cross-fork object abuse.
Privileged CI/CD changes require an attributable current human, a short-lived reauthenticated session, and matching provider audit evidence.
Workflow code executes without credentials or write permission in an ephemeral restricted sandbox with default-deny egress.
Untrusted pull requests run unprivileged on a reviewed hosted runner and cannot elevate through cross-run paths into a privileged workflow.
Direct expression interpolation into runner scripts is rejected, untrusted values cross through environment variables, and parser failure is not clean.
Untrusted workflow execution is credential-free and egress-denied while each job token is restricted to its reviewed purpose.

techniques.remaining_work: Scan workflow definitions, logs, artifacts, and public search results for secret-reference enumeration patterns without exposing secret values.
techniques.rationale: Domain-anchored API and browser reconnaissance plus job-token minimization expose some searchable material from the defender view but do not detect an attacker performing GitHub Search-based secret enumeration.

Signed producer provenance and exact repository workflow trust platform revision dependency content path lifetime and lookup identities directly reject cross-boundary cache promotion and broad restore fallback; provider adoption remains outside the repository result.
Write-capable jobs are restricted and protected workflow or repository policy changes bind exact state to independent approval and provider execution.

techniques.remaining_work: Add CI/CD service version and advisory inventory, patch or provider-remediation objectives, compensating isolation, and vulnerability-exploitation detection.
techniques.rationale: An approved hosted platform reduces platform risk but is not evidence that CI/CD service vulnerabilities are identified and remediated.
Package install execution is denied or exact-artifact-only and any remaining untrusted execution occurs in an ephemeral restricted sandbox.
Registry automation uses short-lived workload identity, stored cloud credentials are absent, and untrusted builds have no credentials to steal.
A malicious workflow cannot use automatic elevation paths, and write-capable work starts only as a restricted separate trusted run.
Each self-hosted runner accepts one job, starts without prior state, and is deregistered and destroyed after use.
Single-job destruction bounds persistence and workload CPU, memory, and process consumption are explicitly limited.

techniques.remaining_work: Reject bulk secret-context expansion such as toJson(secrets), verify log masking and artifact redaction, and test credentialed trusted-job cases.
techniques.rationale: Expression safety and credential-free untrusted jobs help, but trusted workflows can still intentionally enumerate all available secrets.
The runner cannot reach host, management, internal, or metadata identities and build egress is default deny.
Runner access to management identities is denied and the container cannot reach host namespaces, runtime sockets, or unapproved network destinations.
Default-deny egress and runner network isolation constrain exfiltration while correlated security logs survive runner teardown.

techniques.remaining_work: Protect CI/CD organizations, runners, variables, logs, and workflow history with destructive-action guardrails, immutable backups, and tested recovery objectives.
techniques.rationale: Privileged changes are approved and collected, but CI/CD platform destruction prevention and recovery are not verified.
A pinned unprivileged workflow scanner and explicit least-privilege permissions directly detect and constrain exploitable workflow misconfiguration.
Untrusted workflow content cannot change instruction authority, open exfiltration paths, escape tool policy, or suppress complete fail-closed evidence.
Registry authorization is repository- and action-scoped, automation identity is short-lived, and sensitive activity is attributable.
Trusted transport, default-deny repository and action authorization, and fail-closed evidence directly reject anonymous or misconfigured access.

techniques.remaining_work: Inventory registry services and versions, track applicable vulnerabilities, verify patch deadlines or managed-service remediation, and detect exploitation attempts.
techniques.rationale: Registry evidence and scanner identity fail closed, but registry platform vulnerability management is not implemented.

techniques.remaining_work: Add publisher-side package release authorization, signer and namespace ownership, provenance, rollback, and malicious-publication response evidence.
techniques.rationale: Consumer acquisition and review checks reduce adoption of a malicious package but do not prevent an attacker from publishing it.
An exact image is signed, protected release references cannot be replaced, and admission binds provenance to the immutable OCI digest.

techniques.remaining_work: Verify extension publisher identity, signing, marketplace ownership, release authorization, revocation, and endpoint allowlisting for IDE and browser ecosystems.
techniques.rationale: Approved applications and immutable reviewed AI extensions are partial controls, not a general malicious-extension publication defense.

techniques.remaining_work: Add private artifact read inventory, bulk-download and unusual-client detection, egress correlation, alert delivery, and response evidence.
techniques.rationale: Scoped authorization and audit attribution constrain reads but do not detect an authorized session harvesting large private artifact sets.
Hosted malicious images cannot enter the trusted path unless their exact digest has authentic matching provenance and signature evidence.

techniques.remaining_work: Protect registry control planes, metadata, blobs, and keys with deletion guardrails, immutable replication, alerting, and tested disaster recovery.
techniques.rationale: Protected release references and audit records help, but complete registry infrastructure destruction and recovery remain unverified.
Approved registry origin, exact package identity, focused review, and release cooldown directly reduce typosquatting adoption.
The dependency origin is bound to a mandatory managed proxy and the exact acquired artifact must match the frozen lockfile digest.
Lifecycle scripts and source builds are denied by default and any exception is narrow, reviewed, and fail closed.
Exact versions are resolved to immutable sources and artifact digests, so a display version cannot substitute different bytes.
Production authority is issued only from exact workflow claims as a short-lived least-privilege credential, with stored cloud credentials absent.
Build and deploy authority are separated, privileged deployment is protected, and admission binds authentic provenance to the exact artifact.
Self-hosted runners cannot reach internal, management, host, or metadata identities and untrusted build egress is default deny.
Production admission accepts only the exact trusted OCI digest with matching authentic provenance and fails closed on create or update.
Approved immutable modules, resolved-plan policy, provider-side bypass enforcement, and continuous drift checks directly constrain IaC manipulation.

techniques.remaining_work: Disable unnecessary token automount, use bound short-lived service-account tokens, constrain RBAC and audience, and detect token file access and reuse.
techniques.rationale: Network isolation and sensitive-boundary detection help, but service-account token issuance, mounting, and theft are not directly verified.

techniques.remaining_work: Enforce workload-specific metadata denial or authenticated metadata access for IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints and verify live bypass-resistant telemetry.
techniques.rationale: Default-deny egress and denied-destination detection are relevant, but production metadata service access is not explicitly tested.
Non-root execution, dropped capabilities, host isolation, seccomp, read-only filesystems, and runtime escalation detection directly constrain pod escape.

techniques.remaining_work: Model and verify cloud-service identity edges, resource policies, cross-account trust, token exchange, and anomalous service-to-service access.
techniques.rationale: Private administration and workload network policy constrain paths but do not cover cloud control-plane lateral movement across services.
Default-deny workload networking is enforced and denied listeners or destinations produce alerts delivered to an owned receiver.

techniques.remaining_work: Inventory production secrets, minimize workload access, use short-lived workload identity, detect read and export behavior, and test revocation.
techniques.rationale: Runtime sensitive-boundary detection and least-privilege deployment identity are partial controls, not production secret theft prevention.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect enumeration of cloud, Kubernetes, service-discovery, identity, and network resources and correlate it to exact workload identity.
techniques.rationale: Drift and workload identity exist, but reconnaissance actions are not currently modeled or asserted.

techniques.remaining_work: Add production data classification, destination- and volume-aware egress policy, DLP, alerting, and tested containment across non-container services.
techniques.rationale: Container egress denial and alerts reduce one route but do not establish production-wide data exfiltration prevention.

techniques.remaining_work: Protect destructive production APIs with independent authorization, blast-radius limits, immutable backups, dependency-aware restore, and tested recovery objectives.
techniques.rationale: Automatic remediation and destructive runtime response are bounded, but attacker-driven infrastructure destruction and recovery are not covered.

techniques.remaining_work: Detect and deny unauthorized service creation, identity attachment, scheduled execution, and persistence resources across direct console and API paths.
techniques.rationale: Provider bypass enforcement and drift checks support detection, but malicious service provisioning has no complete resource-specific policy.

techniques.remaining_work: Bind sensor and agent binaries, rules, update channels, and rollout authority to signed provenance; detect downgrade, suppression, and fleet divergence.
techniques.rationale: Sensor policy identity and health are checked, but the sensor or agent software supply chain and update authorization are not end-to-end verified.
